chapter: Billy Berg's, Granz and Nat Cole
title: Strayhorn in Los Angeles and the 1941 ASCAP ban
summary: Willard explains the ASCAP radio strike when Strayhorn and Mercer Ellington supplied new material to the Ellington band.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Was Billy staying here in Los Angeles when the band wasn't?
Or was he only here when the band was here at that point?
Well, the band was here at that point, I think, wasn't it. Jump For Joy...

Well, Jump For Joy opened July 10th, 1941, and "A Train" was recorded in February, I think. The band was playing here in January and February at the Casa Mañana in January and February of 1941. I can run and get my discography real quick. I think it was February that "A Train" was recorded, because that was during the ASCAP

strike or ban, and the band couldn't play... They had all these live remotes going, and they couldn't play any ASCAP tunes on the radio during that period, so that's when they changed themes and a whole lot of new material came into the book that Billy wrote. Because Duke couldn't write anything at that point. That's also when a lot of things showed up by Mercer Ellington.
Oh, that's right. [SINGS REFRAIN OF "Things Ain'T What They Used To Be"]. That's Mercer, too, isn't it; "Things Ain'T What They Used To Be".

Well, that's when it suddenly appeared. And a lot of things came out with Mercer's byline, or Mercer's composer credit. But during that period from January 1st until I think October, no ASCAP music could be broadcast.
That's when BMI came into being, too, wasn't it.

That's right. Because the radio stations wouldn't make their peace... They wouldn't pay the fees that ASCAP was demanding. So nothing was licensed, no ASCAP material was licensed to be played during that period. Although I have an aircheck of Duke and Herb Jeffries doing a guest shot plugging...no, it was during a tribute to...I can't remember now...a Black actor... Duke plays "Chocolate
Shake" and something else that he was written, and "Chocolate Shake" he said was from his... He was plugging Jump For Joy, which was to open the following month. It's a June aircheck.
